examples.pie: h₁yód ḱr̥dés gʷm̥yéti tód ḱḗr h₁r̥sḱéti. h₁wésu wékʷos déh₃rom.
examples.en: What comes from the heart reaches the heart. A good word is a gift.

examples.pie: h₁yós gʰóstipoteyey dʰugh₂térm̥ déh₃eti déh₃royh₁ bʰoréyēti.
examples.en: Whoever gives a daughter to a lord, he shall bring two gifts.

examples.pie: h₁yós déh₃nom dédeh₃eti déh₃etor déh₃rom tósmey.
examples.en: Whoever gives a gift, a gift shall be given to him.

examples.pie: h₁wr̥Héwih₂ nos dʰéǵʰōm bʰéreti.
examples.en: The broad earth bears us.

examples.pie: mértis h₂nérm̥ lémbʰeti logʰéyetu tósyo swésōr tóm dʰǵʰémi.
examples.en: If death seizes a man, let his sister lay him on the earth.

examples.pie: sóh₂wl̥ dʰéǵʰōm lowkéyeti. lówksneh₂ kʷsépm̥ lowkéyeti.
examples.en: The sun lights up the earth. The moon lights up the night.

examples.pie: kʷsépi kʷid ḱlḗm. só wĺ̥kʷos? só ǵʰḗr. h₂ŕ̥tḱōd bʰéyh₂m̥. h₂ŕ̥tḱōs ǵʰiméni ssénti nu-kʷe ǵʰéyōm h₁ésti. péh₂wr̥ h₂éle ssdʰí-kʷe. bʰéwdʰēsi? bʰéwdʰōh₂ nókʷtm̥-kʷe te pér h₂léksōh₂. nu sésoh₂ h₂stéres nos spéḱyonti.
examples.en: I heard something in the night. Is it a wolf? That is a hedgehog. I was afraid of a bear. Bears sleep in winter, and now it is winter. Feed the fire, and sleep. Will you stay awake? I shall stay awake, and I shall guard you through the night. Then I shall sleep; the stars are watching us.

examples.pie: kʷís ḱóymosyo h₁esh₂ós h₁ésti? h₃rḗǵs ḱóymosyo h₁esh₂ós h₁ésti.
examples.en: Who is the master of the village? The king is the master of the village.

examples.pie: kʷís ph₂wéns ǵn̥h₁yétor ḱóymōd-kʷe úd h₁éyti? h₁ím kʷis ǵʰóstoh₁ ne kapyéti. dʰuh₂mós.
examples.en: Who is born of fire and goes up from the home? No one holds him in the hand. Smoke.

examples.pie: h₁yód dʰuh₂mós h₁ésti péh₂wr̥ h₁ésti. dʰuh₂mós ḱóymōd úd gʷm̥sḱéti. péh₂wr̥ ne ḱéletor.
examples.en: If there is smoke, there is fire. Smoke comes up from the home. Fire does not hide itself.

root.gloss: to turn (end-over-end); to revolve around, and therefore to sojourn, to dwell

examples.pie: gʰrómosyo deywós HeHḱúns h₁éḱwons h₂éǵet. gʰrómos yéh₂t n̥bʰrós-kʷe tóm sékʷeto. tósyo kʷékʷlōs kʷl̥h₁ént. h₁ógʷʰis tóm kʷéḱt. nu só trémt só-kʷe ní sérpet. gʷʰént h₁ógʷʰim. wédōr térkh₂t. nu só h₂epó léytt.
examples.en: The god of thunder drove swift horses. Thunder went, and the rain-cloud followed him. His wheels turned. Then the serpent saw him, and trembled, and crept down. He slew the serpent. He released the waters. Then he went away.

examples.pie: gʰóstipotey kʷid léh₂kt. só h₂énh₁mos stégos Hyowdʰéyeti. só ne wĺ̥kʷos? ḱwónes th₂kéh₁yonti. l̥gʰdʰí ssdʰí-kʷe h₁eǵóh₂ bʰéwdʰoh₂. túH n̥smé h₂léksesi. h₂ewsér h₂éḱh₃omes.
examples.en: Host, something made a noise. That is the wind; it is shaking the roof. Is it not a wolf? The dogs are silent. Lie down and sleep; I am awake. You guard us. At dawn let us eat.

root.gloss: to swell (with milk); to be swollen, fat

examples.pie: kr̥snṓy péyh₂tu déh₃t só-kʷe pl̥h₁nós h₁ést.
examples.en: He gave the nourishment to the black one, and it was full.

examples.pie: nu wósr̥ gʷegʷóme gʷʰért-kʷe. nu snígʷʰs tinéh₁ti wódr̥ drémt. gʷénh₂es péyh₂tu pékʷonti wĺ̥kʷōs n̥ḱént. h₂éweyes nisdóns démonti. nu lewkóm n̥sméy priHóm h₁syéh₁s. téwe léwkesi gʷíh₃woyh₁me.
examples.en: Spring has come, and it became warm. The snow melts, the water runs. The women cook the nourishing food. The wolves vanish. The birds build nests. Bright one, may you be dear to us. May we live in your light!

examples.pie: kʷís h₁ógʷʰim gʷʰént? wiHrós h₁ógʷʰim h₂ḱm̥néh₁ gʷʰént. h₁ógʷʰis gʷṓs ḱélet wiHrós-kʷe tóns spért. nu méǵh₂ ḱléwos h₁áyto. kʷís h₁éy h₁ést? h₁éy h₁suḱléwēs h₁ést.
examples.en: Who slew the serpent? A hero slew the serpent with a stone. The serpent was hiding the cows, and the hero freed them. Then he received great fame. Who was he? He was Of-Good-Fame.

examples.pie: h₁yód sh₂itós bʰéwgeti h₁ím-kʷe kʷis lémbʰeti h₁ím h₂ew wédʰetu. h₁yós sh₂itóm spéreti só dwóh₁ sh₂itóh₁ déh₃tu h₁óytom-kʷe h₁épetor. sh₂itósyo wósn̥ déḱm̥ gʷówes.
examples.en: If a bound one flees and a man seizes him, let him lead him back. Whoever frees a bound one, let him give two bound ones and he shall take the oath. The price of a bound one is ten cattle.

examples.pie: h₂ékʷeh₂es méh₂teres ḱluté. nu h₁yéh₂es h₂ówins h₂élete. h₁yéh₂es móri h₁ité h₁ógʷʰis usmé Hwért. pérkʷunos-ge usmé spért pró-kʷe gʷh₂té. mē tr̥sih₁té stérgete nos.
examples.en: Waters, mothers, hear! You who now nourish the sheep, you who go to the sea. The serpent enclosed you; Perkʷunos indeed set you free, and you went forth. Do not dry up; protect us.

examples.pie: ḱéywe te bʰréh₂ter ne mérsoh₂. ḱm̥tóm-ge wetsóns h₁opéyont. wetsṓs sph₁rṓs túH-kʷe néḱus. sweh₂dú h₁éysōm mḗms ne h₂éḱh₃oh₂. kréwh₂s toy nékʷtsu widéh₁yoh₂. bʰréh₂ter te deywṓs memnih₁ént.
examples.en: Dear brother, I will not forget you. They gave a hundred calves. The calves are fat, and you are dead. I will not eat their sweet flesh. In the nights I see your blood. May the gods remember you, brother.

examples.pie: h₂éti gʷegʷómth₂e. kʷíd moréyes? h₂ŕ̥tḱom. bʰréh₂teres moy h₁ím dṓm bʰéronti. h₂ŕ̥tḱos sph₁rós. h₁ésyo nos skéwHtis ǵʰyémi stégeti h₁ésyo-kʷe sélpos tinh₁més. h₂ŕ̥tḱos te ne dénḱt? skélos moy dénḱt kéh₂ilos h₁ésmi.
examples.en: You have come back! What did you kill? A bear. My brothers are carrying it home. The bear is fat! Its skin will cover us in winter, and we will melt its fat. Did the bear not bite you? It bit my leg, but I am whole.

examples.pie: wiHróns péḱuh₂ ph₂dʰí.
examples.en: Protect the men and the livestock!

examples.pie: h₂éyos h₁rudʰéh₁dʰi h₂éyos h₁ólos bʰuHdʰí. nu mē bʰéyds ḱléwos wiHrṓy h₁syéh₁t.
examples.en: Copper, become red! Copper, become an awl. Do not split. May there be fame for the man.

examples.pie: polh₁éwes péḱesi lewbʰṓs. lewbʰós h₂égʰesi ǵn̥nh₃tór. wíHre lewbʰóm mē dʰrugʰyés.
examples.en: In wealth many are dear. In distress the dear one is known. Do not deceive your dear one.

examples.en: Man, you took the larger share! I was first, and they wounded me. They wounded me too. Look at my leg! Then let us divide the plunder in two. Who will divide it? Let the wise old man divide it. I will heed him. And let us two not fight.

examples.pie: h₁yód gʰósteyes h₂ḱh₃ént mr̥tóybʰos loypéh₂m sikʷdʰí. tóns kh₂n̥ménh₁ gʷr̥nHdʰí. gʷoh₂móm linkʷdʰí ḱóymom h₁idʰí méwde-kʷe.
examples.en: When the guests have eaten, pour out the remainder for the dead. Praise them with a song. Leave the altar, go home, and rejoice.

examples.pie: moysóm gʷoh₂móm wédʰe. h₁ím ḱéstroh₁ skl̥Hdʰí. h₁ésyo h₁ésh₂r̥ dʰǵʰémi sikʷdʰí. mḗms gʷrúsu pékʷe. dʰh₁séy pr̥h₂wóm bʰoh₂góm dh₃dʰí sélpos-kʷe ph₂wéni h₁éwse. nu h₁léwdʰeyes mḗms h₁édonti.
examples.en: Lead the ram to the altar. Slit it open with the knife. Pour out its blood on the earth. Cook the meat on spits. Give the first share to the god, and burn the fat in the fire. Then let the people eat the meat.

examples.pie: nu dʰugʰyéh₁t h₂éǵros gʷunuyéh₁t-kʷe h₂éǵmn̥.
examples.en: Now may the field be productive, and may the flock grow.

examples.pie: kʷíd kóslom ḱéleti wésmn̥-kʷe ne h₁ésti? só h₁iHn̥yós h₁ésti.

examples.pie: wih₁rósyo suHnús ḱóymoy ǵeǵónh₁e.
examples.en: The man's son has been born in the household.

examples.pie: wih₁róm dʰǵʰyés ǵnéh₃m̥. kʷís h₁éy? h₁éy ḱóymōd poh₂imḗn. h₁éy h₁wésus wih₁rós? h₁éy moy ḱéywos. wr̥h₁énm̥ moy déh₃t. nu h₁éy priHós.
examples.en: Yesterday I met a man. Who is he? He is a shepherd from the village. Is he a good man? He is dear to me. He gave me a lamb. Then he is a friend!

examples.pie: sérpont HéHḱew h₂éngʷʰey lóyseh₂i l̥gʰdʰí. nu h₂ówins poh₂iménm̥-kʷe mē h₁r̥sḱés. nu ḱwṓ bʰéwdʰeti nu twé kʷéḱt. h₂epó sérpe nu bʰudʰménm̥ ní h₁idʰí. wih₁rós kʷis ǵʰwḗr-kʷe mē n̥ḱyéh₁t.
examples.en: Swift snake, creeping in the furrow, lie down! Do not go to the sheep or the shepherd. Now the dog is awake, he sees you. Creep away, now go down to the bottom. May no one be lost, man and beast alike.

pie-neo-smeymn.gloss: joke, jest: something to laugh at

examples.pie: ḱwṓ toy pérdetor. ne pérdetor. túH pérdeth₂er. dʰrugʰyési me. príHe smḗymi. tód sméymn̥.
examples.en: Your dog is farting! He is not farting! You are farting! You are deceiving me! I am laughing, friend. That is a joke.

examples.pie: sméymn̥ moy wéwke. kʷís bʰéh₂ti dn̥ǵʰwéh₂s-kʷe h₁ésmey ne h₁ésti? h₁eǵóh₂. smḗymi. tód sméymn̥ h₁wésu.
examples.en: Tell me a joke! Who speaks, and has no tongue? I do! I laugh. That joke is good.

examples.pie: sméymn̥ moy wéwke. súHs h₃rēǵés ḱóymom gʷéh₂t. h₃rḗǵs wéwket kʷís túH? súHs h₂éǵt h₁eǵóh₂ toy néwos h₃rḗǵs. néwos h₃rḗǵs.
examples.en: Tell me a joke! A pig went to the king's home. The king said: who are you? The pig said: I am your new king! A new king!

source.name: coinage
source.note: Result noun in -mn̥ 'what is laughed at' from smey- 'laugh, smile' (smḗyti; Ved. smáyate, OCS směxъ).
